title: Skilled Worker visa for the United Kingdom: a sponsored job in an eligible occupation, usually paying at least £41,700 a year and the going rate, with English at B2

sources.title: Immigration Rules, Appendix Skilled Worker, SW 1.3: the applicant must be aged 18 or over on the date of application
Appendix Skilled Worker, SW 3.3: a person must not be applying for entry clearance as a Skilled Worker as a national or citizen of Afghanistan
Explanatory memorandum to Statement of Changes HC 1691, para. 5.3: Skilled Worker visa applications from main applicants who are nationals of Afghanistan are refused from 26 March 2026
Appendix Skilled Worker, SW 1.2(d), 4.1 and 5.1 to 6.4: a recent Certificate of Sponsorship from a licensed, A-rated sponsor, for a job in an eligible occupation (Appendix Skilled Occupations)
Appendix Skilled Worker, SW 4.2 and the table after SW 4.4, options A to E: at least £41,700 and the going rate; lower floors for a PhD, the Immigration Salary List or a new entrant
Immigration Rules, Appendix Skilled Occupations, Tables 1 to 3: the eligible occupations, skilled to RQF level 6 or above, and their going rates
Appendix Skilled Worker, SW 4.1 and 7.1 to 7.2: English at CEFR level B2 in reading, writing, speaking and listening, shown as Appendix English Language specifies
Explanatory memorandum to Statement of Changes HC 1333, paras. 5.22, 5.23 and 6.4: the Skilled Worker English requirement rises from B1 to B2 for first grants from 8 January 2026
Appendix Skilled Worker, SW 15.2 and 15.3: from abroad, £1,270 held for 28 days, unless the A-rated sponsor certifies it will maintain and accommodate the applicant to that amount
Appendix Skilled Worker, SW 26.3, 29.1, 29.1A, 29.2 and 32A.1 to 32A.2: a dependent partner aged 18 or over and dependent children of a Skilled Worker sponsored for a job in Table 1, 2 or 3
Appendix Skilled Worker, SW 33.2 to 33.4: £285 for a partner, £315 for the first child, £200 for each other child, on top of the worker's funds, unless the sponsor certifies
Appendix Relationship with Partner, RWP 1.1 and 5.1: both partners 18 or over; if not married or civil partners, a relationship similar to marriage for at least 2 years
Appendix Children, CHI 1.1, 1.2, 1A.1 and 3.2: under 18, or older if last granted permission as a dependent child; no independent life; both parents come, unless one has sole responsibility
Immigration Rules, introduction, para. 5C and definitions: not for Irish citizens who need no leave; a partner is a spouse, civil or unmarried partner of 2 years; a parent is not a step-parent
Immigration Act 1971, ss. 1(1), 2(1)(a) and 3ZA(1): British citizens have the right of abode; Irish citizens do not require leave to enter or remain
Age of Legal Capacity (Scotland) Act 1991, s. 6: a person born on 29 February has their anniversary on 1 March in a year that is not a leap year
Family Law Reform Act 1969, s. 9(1): a person attains an age at the commencement of the anniversary of their birth

requirements.title: Not a British or Irish citizen: they live and work in the UK without a visa
Not applying from abroad as a citizen of Afghanistan only, refused since 26 March 2026; someone living in the UK who switches from another permission: possible

assessments.title: A sponsored job from a licensed, A-rated employer in an eligible occupation (RQF 6 or above), paying at least £41,700 a year and the going rate; a new entrant: £33,400 and 70% of it
English at level B2 in reading, writing, speaking and listening, through an approved test, a degree taught in English or citizenship of a majority English-speaking country
Savings held for 28 days: £1,270 for the worker, plus £285 for a partner, £315 for the first child and £200 for each other child, unless the sponsor certifies it will maintain them

dependents.title: Partner aged 18 or over, after 2 years in a relationship similar to marriage; a shorter one, which may be a civil partnership: possible
Children under 18 whose other parent comes too, unless the principal has sole responsibility; an adult child who depends on the principal: possible, only after UK permission as their child
